old.note: Relocated base rows of the integration zero-literal scan (README "Reviewed occurrences", "Relocated base rows"). A record continues one base ledger row (row) whose source line a block B edit changed after the base without touching the row's span: line, column, endLine and endColumn give the post-base position of the same occurrence and lineSha256 the SHA-256 of the post-base line; file, form, entry, family, literal, key and the span length are the row's, and rule, category, consumer, targetRef and disposition repeat its classification. edit names the block B commit and every base row of the same base line whose span the edit replaced, with the post-base columns and the SHA-256 of the replacement: the post-base line is the base line with those spans substituted, and the row's columns move by the length change of the replacements before it. The integration scan (derive/reviewed.mjs) and the probe rescan (probe-expectations.json#/probe2/trackedRescan) pair an occurrence with the base row through the record's key (masked file, form, entry, literal, column, endColumn, line span and lineSha256) exactly as through the row's base key, and a row pairs with one occurrence at most through all its keys; the line number is not part of the key. A relocation is not a review: the row keeps its rule, disposition and post-migration obligations, a business literal is never reviewed, and any change of the post-base line voids the key. verifiedAt names the tree and the file bytes at which the record was verified; derive/base-check.mjs checks each record against the base line of its row and the seal test against the base row and the current file.
